run.brief: Generate one independent, lossless 100-observation challenge portfolio from the semantic saturation audit without reading prior candidate portfolios or the registry until all surfaces are frozen. Preserve affirmative, ambivalent, adverse, malformed, and wildcard forms; use only atlas IDs in tags; embody current code truth and conditional artifact horizons; analyze audience trust, fear, control, burden, power, access, cost, refusal, and unavailable mechanisms; do not rank, select, screen availability, or repair overlaps.
notes: Exact user prompt SHA-256 is recorded; prompt_path is null because the prompt was supplied inline and no prompt file was created.

Exact inline prompt (the recorded SHA-256 covers this UTF-8 text plus one final LF): You own only /Users/deepfates/Hacking/github/deepfates/dspy_elixir/identity/inbox/20-semantic-power-b.json. You are not alone in the codebase: do not revert, stage, commit, or modify another file. Create independent semantic/power challenge wave B as one schema-valid portfolio of exactly 100 contiguous candidates and 20 wildcards. Follow the exact ten-row counts, primary-strategy quotas, total 50 affirmative/25 ambivalent/25 adverse, total 40 current/40 horizon/20 both, embodiments, provisional lenses, and anti-convergence constraints in identity/reports/saturation-semantic-audit.md.

Isolation: read the product boundary, implementation/docs, atlas, portfolio schema, and semantic audit only. Before freezing all 100 surfaces, do NOT read identity/inbox candidate files, registry, enrichments, scores, or any report containing candidate surfaces. Provisional semantic/audience concepts are challenge labels in notes only; all candidate tags must use current atlas IDs. After freezing, mechanically compare normalized IDs against the accepted-only identity/registry.jsonl, record all overlaps without replacement, inspect every record, and validate with DSEx.IdentityCheckpoint plus JSON schema.

Correct wave-A weaknesses: never claim immutable rollback/durable persistence, haptics, councils, redress institutions, public governance, carbon accounting, legal guarantees, accessibility validation, native-speaker review, or user research. Ground every current embodiment in a specific shipped API/behavior verified in code; keep horizon claims conditional across the specified artifact classes. Each candidate needs candidate-specific trust/fear/control/burden analysis for actual audiences; concrete actor/action/access-path/cost/unavailable-mechanism power/refusal notes; non-boilerplate current and horizon embodiments; pronunciation, grammar, etymology, concerns, architecture lenses, and precise scope/stance/challenge-row notes. Do not rank, shortlist, availability-check, repair overlaps, or select. Preserve adverse and malformed ideas. Record exact generator/model/method/prompt provenance and honest limitations. Validate, report the file and checks, and make no commit.

The runtime identified the generator as OpenAI Codex based on GPT-5; no more specific model build, reasoning-effort label, or stable agent ID was exposed, so those unavailable fields are not invented.

Before all 100 surfaces were frozen, no candidate inbox file, registry, enrichment, score, favorite, or report other than the required saturation semantic audit was read. Honest independence limitation: that required audit itself quotes examples of prior surfaces; no underlying candidate record or additional surface report was inspected.
Provisional semantic and audience concepts are challenge labels in candidate notes only; all territories, strategies, audiences, and architectures use atlas version 1 IDs.

No availability, trademark, marketplace, native-language, cultural-community, accessibility, legal, security, or participant research was performed. Pronunciations, cultural concerns, and audience reactions are hypotheses for later evidence, not validated findings.

Current embodiments were grounded against shipped DSEx public or implementation APIs. Horizon embodiments are conditional across instructions, demonstrations, tool descriptions, retrieval policies, playbooks, schemas, code fragments, and configuration.

This raw portfolio makes no ranking, shortlist, selection, deletion, repair, compatibility mark, official status, privacy, security, safety, accessibility, consent, fairness, ownership, legal compliance, healing, or improvement guarantee.
